title: What selects the physical evolution after plasticity loses ellipticity?
summary: Classical localization theory can identify loss of ellipticity, but after that point a local plasticity model may no longer select a unique finite-width, mesh-independent continuation. What physical limiting law selects the observed evolution?

statement.lead: For an incremental elastoplastic tangent C^ep, localization onset can be detected by loss of acoustic-tensor invertibility,
statement.after: The open problem begins after this classical criterion: when the local equations cease to select a unique continuation, determine which small-scale physics or limiting principle selects finite band width, propagation, arrest, dissipation and transition to fracture.

why: Loss of ellipticity is where a continuum constitutive law is tested most severely: local softening models can produce vanishing band thickness, mesh-dependent dissipation and nonunique post-bifurcation paths.
Real materials nevertheless form finite-width bands that propagate, arrest, develop internal structure and sometimes turn into cracks.
A predictive post-localization theory would explain the emergent lower-dimensional evolution law rather than prescribe a numerical regularization length.
scope: Primary setting: continuum plasticity after a declared loss-of-ellipticity or related localization instability; shear bands are the canonical example, not the only admissible material system.

Gradient, viscous, thermomechanical, dislocation-based, nonlocal and damage regularizations are treated as candidate small-scale physics whose limiting selection laws must be compared rather than assumed equivalent.
The problem distinguishes localization onset from post-localization evolution, and finite-width regularization from the macroscopic law that remains as the regularizing scale becomes small.

boundary.text: Classical bifurcation and loss-of-ellipticity theory can predict localization onset and orientation for broad constitutive classes; that onset problem is not the open target.

Kinetic-relation theory in phase-transforming solids provides a structural precedent: when continuum balance laws are nonunique, small-scale viscosity/gradient physics can select an effective propagation law.

Many plasticity regularizations already generate finite-width bands, including microstructured, gradient, viscous and dislocation-based models. Their existence does not identify which limiting law is physically selected in a stated material class.
Recent finite-strain gradient plasticity, dislocation/GND-based simulations and rank-one gradient plasticity give increasingly explicit finite-width or geometry-dependent post-localization behavior.

A 2026 nonlinear theory also predicts finite-width shear bands in an athermal amorphous-solid setting, showing that no general website statement should claim that band width itself is wholly unexplained.

The conservative open core is whether physically motivated small-scale regularizations select a unique effective post-localization evolution and whether different regularizations fall into common universality/kinetic classes or select genuinely different macroscopic continuations.

settle: Derive an effective admissibility or kinetic law for a propagating/arresting localized plastic zone as an appropriate regularization scale tends to zero.

Show that a declared class of physically distinct regularizations converges to the same post-localization law, or construct a counterexample proving genuine nonuniqueness between equally admissible small-scale models.
Separate nucleation, propagation, arrest and transition to fracture within one consistent selection framework and validate discriminating predictions experimentally.

progress.title: Finite-width theory sharpens the residual target
progress.text: Recent analytic and gradient-plasticity results show that finite band widths can be predicted in important model classes; the remaining question is the physically selected continuation and limiting law.

progress.title: Dislocation and rank-one gradient models add explicit post-localization regimes
progress.text: Recent work produces finite-width bands and geometry-dependent nucleation/selection in additional classes, making comparison of limiting selection laws increasingly concrete.
